A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Attention Search. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the relocated checklist and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v3 reports original PG-19 training experiments, Llama and Mistral evaluations on RULER and LongBench, latency measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and reports updated PG-19 and latency results plus new token-role distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The token roles, Gumbel-Softmax selection, attention masks, gradient regularization, and distillation objective are retained. The expanded prefill description and new Algorithm 3 document inference without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use PG-19, the same 7,000-instance fine-tuning mixture, RULER, and LongBench. The new token-role analyses use the already studied MultiNews and NarrativeQA datasets; no distinct task or population is added.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: full attention, StreamingLLM, H2O, DuoAttention, SnapKV, AdaKV, ChunkKV, CriticalKV, PyramidKV, and MoA. Newly cited works are not added evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported chunked-prefilling size from 32,000 to 10,000 tokens. Figure 4 also adds 10k and 50k prefill measurement points. The remaining benchmark and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix J and Figures 10–11 examine the distribution of global, local, and sliding-window token roles across Llama layers and heads on two datasets. Existing regularization/window-size ablations and KV-size distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 Section 4.1 reports three seeds and standard-deviation error bars for PG-19, whereas v3 reports single fixed-seed runs. This is a limited expansion of uncertainty reporting. The unchanged v4 checklist still says all experiments ran once, contradicting the new description.

E6.justification: Figures 3–4 contain revised results; Section 4.3 changes the reported 200k-token prefill speedup from 1.83x to 3.0x under revised settings, not a directly comparable performance gain. Figures 10–11 add findings that global and sliding-window roles predominate. Tables 1–8 retain their numerical entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Equations 1–26 are retained. The new soft-threshold discussion is intuitive explanation, and the N/L notation edits in pseudocode do not establish revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: learning token roles end-to-end and reducing KV storage and inference costs while largely preserving model performance.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of regularization as a soft threshold, model weights influencing KV importance, and token-role distributions suggesting predominantly short- or long-range correlations. Appendix A also explains how query-dependent attention patterns complicate token eviction.

D1.justification: v4 adds cache-update pseudocode in Appendix E, explains separate prefill computation for global/local and sliding-window tokens, and discloses FlashInfer RoPE and RMSNorm kernels. Existing training details, data preparation instructions, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 expands the comparison with attention-approximation approaches, emphasizing direct loss-based learning and decoding-stage cache reduction. References to GQA, DeepSeek-R1, and FlashInfer are added; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized grammar corrections and explanatory expansions, adds two appendix sections, and moves the checklist before the appendices. The main narrative and existing appendix sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 10–11 are added, Figure 3 gains error bars, and Figure 4 is redrawn with revised axes and plotting ranges. Figures and tables are reflowed, and the author block becomes side-by-side. Other existing figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, v4 adds useful PG-19 uncertainty reporting, inference documentation, and evidence about learned token roles, modestly improving transparency and explanation. The method and main benchmark evidence remain stable. The contradictory single-seed checklist weakens reporting consistency, and the revised latency settings prevent treating the larger speedup as a same-setting improvement.
